heading: Static vs Dynamic Android Intent Fuzzing: A False Negative Analysis
core_technical_idea: Comparing the high false negative rate of static manifest regex matching against runtime Frida intent tracking across execution paths.
composition: Bar chart comparing static regex parsing against dynamic Frida instrumentation false negative rates.
alt_text: Bar chart comparing False Negative Rates between Static Manifest Regex Matching and Dynamic Frida Taint Tracking, showing a drop from 42% to 5%.
caption: Shifting from static manifest regex to runtime Frida instrumentation reduces the False Negative Rate (FNR) from 42% down to 5%.

heading: Applying Precision-Recall Formulas to Empirical Security Metrics
core_technical_idea: Empirical comparison of Static Regex Analysis, Dynamic Frida Fuzzing, and Hybrid Framework across Precision, Recall, and False Negative Rates.
must_show: Precision scores for Static (0.20), Dynamic (0.91), and Hybrid (0.85)
Recall (TPR) scores for Static (0.58), Dynamic (0.95), and Hybrid (0.98)
False Negative Rate (FNR) highlighting the 42.5% gap in static analysis
composition: Bar chart comparing the three analysis methods across Precision, Recall, and False Negative Rate metrics.
alt_text: Bar chart comparing Static Regex Analysis, Dynamic Frida Fuzzing, and Hybrid Framework performance across Precision, Recall, and False Negative Rate metrics.
caption: Dynamic and hybrid approaches drastically reduce the 42.5% false negative rate inherent to static regex pattern matching.

heading: Overcoming the Base-Rate Fallacy in Automated CI/CD Pipelines
core_technical_idea: Comparing the posterior probability (precision) of Static Regex versus Dynamic Frida pipeline filters under low vulnerability base-rates (2%).
composition: Bar chart contrasting the actionability and true positive rate of static versus dynamic filters in a CI/CD pipeline.
alt_text: Bar chart comparing the posterior probability of vulnerability given an alert for Static Regex versus Dynamic Frida filters, showing an increase from 2.0% to 43.7%.
caption: Transitioning from static regex to dynamic instrumentation elevates alert precision from noisy 2% to actionable 43.7%.

heading: Plotting False Negative Rate Curves with Python and Matplotlib
core_technical_idea: Comparing False Negative Rates (FNR) between Static Regex Analysis and Dynamic Frida Instrumentation across varying sample sizes, showing dynamic stabilization near 5% versus static high error rates above 40%.
must_show: Static Regex Analysis FNR curve starting near 0.40+ and remaining bounded above 40%
Dynamic Frida Instrumentation FNR curve stabilizing near the 5% target threshold
Sample size axis from 20 to 500 components
composition: Clean quantitative line chart with two distinct series (dashed red for static, solid green for dynamic), a horizontal dotted threshold line, clear axis labels, and a descriptive legend.
alt_text: Line chart comparing the False Negative Rate of Static Regex Analysis versus Dynamic Frida Instrumentation across sample sizes from 20 to 500, highlighting dynamic approach stabilization at 5% FNR.
caption: Empirical FNR performance curves demonstrating how dynamic runtime tracing converges near the 5% target threshold while static regex signatures persist above 40% error rates.
